answer: Each identity declares a compute budget of 685 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision. Because the horizon audit recomputes usage from the meadow history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a trivial one. A farm running 145 keys hence forfeits for 145 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the quartz declaration. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
